chapter: Will Marion Cook and the Southern Syncopated Orchestra
title: Bobby Broussard and the musicians who pooled pay for Cook
summary: Violinist Bobby Broussard formed a band at the Trocadero and the former members donated part of their pay to keep Cook's group going while they found jobs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: But there was something wonderful in the spirit of the Syncopated Orchestra. Certain of the boys then had gotten out and formed bands, small bands.

And we had a wonderful violin player by the name of Bobby Broussard. He went out and he got a top job at the Trocadero Restaurant, which was tops, in those days, and he would take -- and he formed an orchestra of us.
And what they decided to do is simply wonderful. They decided, nobody asked them anything, they decided to donate a certain sum of their salary to the orchestra to Dad Cook's group.
That was awfully nice, you know. That kept us going for awhile, not forever,
Those who left-------- know. We managed to find jobs, individual jobs, and get ourselves together.
